archetype.name: Bubble Team (goaltending-first)
archetype.definition: A .500-ish club whose goalie keeps it in nearly every game while a thin forward group gets outchanced and can't finish, so its playoff case rests on the shooting coming back before the goaltending cools.

report.headline: Skinner keeps it close; a shooting slump turned close games into a losing streak
report.take:
Winnipeg is two seasons removed from a 116-point, first-on-the-site year and one removed from an 82-point collapse. Through 11 games it is on pace for 82 points again. The look has changed, though. Last year's team was mediocre everywhere. This one is a strong goaltending team stapled to an offense ranked 27th. Stuart Skinner has a .911 save % and 5.9 GSAx in eight starts, and that is most of why a club with a 46.1% xGF share and 29.1 shots against a game (25th) sits seventh in goals allowed.

The season turned on finishing. The Jets put 29.2 shots a game on net, ninth in the league. Yet they score on just 8.4% of them, 30th and nearly three points under the league's 11.3%. The last five games are the whole story in miniature: 0-3-2, 1.8 goals a game, every one a one-goal loss and two of them in overtime. The defense allowed 2.8 a game in that stretch, the same as its season rate. Nothing broke at the back. The goals just stopped.

The numbers hide two things in opposite directions. The shooting drought is mostly noise and should lift. Kyle Connor (9 goals on 49 shots) and Cole Perfetti (6 goals) are finishing fine. The rest of the forward group is not: Mark Scheifele has 2 goals on 25 shots, Gabriel Vilardi 1 on 20, and Dawson Mercer none on 24. That kind of spread regresses upward. The worry runs the other way. Underneath, this team is outchanced at 5-on-5, and its 5-on-5 PDO of 101.6 says even-strength results are already a touch flattering. The forward grade is a D and the blueline a C-, so Skinner is covering for a lot. Josh Morrissey has appeared in only 4 of 11 games, which leaves Neal Pionk carrying nearly 25 minutes.

Where it heads depends on which regression comes first. If the depth forwards start converting while Skinner holds, this is a fringe wild-card team. If Skinner drifts toward average before that happens, a skater group with these shot-share numbers looks a lot like last year's.

strengths.title: Skinner is stealing goals
strengths.body: The team's 5.6 Goalies GSAx ranks seventh, and nearly all of it is Skinner's. That gives an outshot team a top-ten goals-against rank. His form is real so far, but an eight-start sample of above-expected goaltending is the most fragile thing on this sheet. Clay Stevenson has been below average in his three starts.

strengths.title: Shot volume says goals are coming
strengths.body: Ninth in shots on goal a game but 30th in shooting %: that pairing rarely lasts. Most of the drought sits with depth forwards like Scheifele, Vilardi and Mercer, who are shooting well below any normal level. Expect scoring to climb even if the chance quality doesn't.

strengths.title: Connor and Perfetti driving it
strengths.body: Connor ranks fifth among 120 left wings and Perfetti seventh among 230 centers. Between them they have ten of the team's power-play points. They are the reason the offense isn't even worse, and their production looks like genuine form rather than hot shooting alone.

concerns.title: Outchanced at even strength
concerns.body: A 46.1% expected-goals share (24th) and a 48% Corsi say the Jets spend more time defending than attacking at 5-on-5. That is a skater problem the D grade for forwards and C- for the blueline both confirm. It is the part of the record least likely to fix itself.

concerns.title: Too many shots allowed
concerns.body: At 29.1 shots against a game, 25th and above the league average, the defense relies on Skinner to turn volume into a good goals-against number. Opposing defensemen are also producing more than expected against Winnipeg (rank 25 vs defensemen). That points to point shots and coverage gaps, not bad luck.

concerns.title: Depth scoring has vanished
concerns.body: Beyond Connor and Perfetti, the forward group is barely scoring. Vilardi is minus-5 and Viggo Björck has no points in 14 minutes a night. The slump should ease, but the bottom-six's poor tab ranks suggest a ceiling on how much.

trend.note: A three-game win streak to open was followed by five straight losses. In that stretch the offense dried up to 1.8 goals a game while goals against held flat.

weekAhead.headline: Four road games, Carolina included, to end a scoring drought
weekAhead.body:
One home game against Florida, then Tampa, Florida again, Carolina and Montréal on the road. Every opponent ranks higher on the site, and all four out-possess Winnipeg on the season. Carolina is the steepest test: second on the site, first in shots on goal a game and fourth in shots allowed. It is exactly the opponent that exposes a team that gives up volume.

The opening is in the opposing nets. Florida, Tampa and Montréal all rank in the bottom third in save %, and Carolina is middling. For a team shooting 8.4%, a week against soft goaltending is the most likely place for the drought to break. Without Skinner at his best, though, the shot-share gap makes a losing week the base case.

keyMatchups.title: Carolina's shot machine vs Skinner
keyMatchups.body: Carolina leads the league in shots per game and holds a 60% expected-goals share. Winnipeg already allows plenty of shots. Skinner will likely need his best night of the week to make this one close.

keyMatchups.title: Weak goaltending across the slate
keyMatchups.body: Florida's .883 and Tampa's .884 save % sit 24th and 23rd, and Montréal is 21st. If Winnipeg keeps generating its usual shot volume, these are the nets where the finishing should finally turn.

keyMatchups.title: Centers against Florida, Connor against Montréal
keyMatchups.body: Florida's defense lets centers outscore their norms (rank 25), a spot for Perfetti and Scheifele. Montréal is generous to wingers (rank 26), which sets up Connor.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Scheifele, Vilardi and Mercer start scoring against the Panthers' and Lightning's weak goaltending, or the offense keeps leaning on Connor alone.

restOfSeason.body:
Two things should move toward the middle. The 8.4% shooting is far too low for a top-ten shot team and will rise. Skinner's goals-saved pace is unlikely to hold over a full workload, and Stevenson has been below average when he plays. Those roughly offset, which leaves the underlying team: outchanced at 5-on-5, thin up front, average on special teams. That profile looks a lot like the 82-point side of last season. The goaltending gives it a somewhat higher floor.

I'd project offense recovering to around 2.7 to 3.0 goals a game and the goals-against rate drifting up slightly as Skinner normalizes. That points to a finish in the mid-to-high 80s in points, short of the Central's playoff line unless the chance share improves. Morrissey's availability is the most obvious internal lever, since the blueline is thin behind Pionk.
swingFactors: Josh Morrissey's availability on the blueline

confidence.note: Only 11 games, and shooting and save % are noisy this early. The shot-share and history signals are consistent with each other.
